thread:
maya: quick thought — we should add a region+tier aware roaming policy for Dedicated -> Hosted spillover. current behaviour is too blunt: it either rejects or blindly routes which leaks isolation guarantees for some enterprise customers.

sam: +1. do we have a contract list anywhere? iirc legal wants explicit opt-in/out for 'hosted' fallback. customers on strict isolation should always reject, not roam.

liam: curious about cost signal too — if we route to hosted during a spike we need to show delta to billing so sales/customer success can predict overages. not just a silent fallback.

olivia: UX note: console should expose a per-tenant toggle: `allow_spillover` and `spillover_mode` with options {strict-reject, best-effort, grace-with-quota}. also a telemetry tab showing "spillover_events", "spillover_cost_delta", "hosted_latency_p95".

maya: proposed policy shape (very small config example):
```yaml
routing_policy:
  primary: dedicated
  fallback:
    hosted:
      enabled: true
      max_percent_of_qps: 25
      allowed_tiers: ["standard", "trial"]
      require_consent: true
      preservation: "kvcache,model_variant_stickiness"
```
we still need to handle region compatibility & model variants (eg quantized variant hosted fallback vs full fp16 dedicated).

sam: for customers flagged as `legal_restrict=true` we should override to `fallback.hosted.enabled=false`. simple. but there are gray cases (customer wants hosted but only in specific regions). need region list too.

elaine: telemetry considerations: add tags `tenant_id`, `primary_region`, `fallback_region`, `model_variant_in`, `model_variant_out`. metrics: `spillover_attempts`, `spillover_success`, `spillover_rejects (policy)`, `spillover_latency_delta_ms`. Also surface traces for a sampled set — link them in console.

infra-bot: routing-config linter run — found no global `allowed_tiers` on 3 policies, flagged as WARN on staging.

liam: rolling this out needs a canary. propose: 1% tenants with non-strict contracts, 12 hour canary, enforce metric assertions: spillover_success_rate > 95%, error_rate delta < 0.2%, p95_hosted_latency < 2x dedicated_p95. If thresholds fail, auto-roll back.

olivia: UI/UX: add an action to "preview spillover impact" that simulates routing with historical qps and shows projected cost. people will use that before flipping the flag. tiny mock: link to a modal with cost slider.

maya: model variant compatibility: we must implement an automated compatibility matrix — hosted fallback can only use variants that preserve functional guarantees (same tokenizer, same EOS behavior). fallback should annotate responses with `x-fallback-reason` header and `x-fallback-variant` so downstream can detect subtle diffs.

sam: regarding logs/privacy: when we route to hosted for a tenant that opted-in, ensure we honor PII redaction policies. also KMS key selection for embeddings if spilled.

elaine: telemetry query examples:
```
select count(*) from spillover_events where tenant_id = 'T-123' and day >= current_date - 7;
```
and Grafana panels: spillover by region (stacked), top tenants by spillover cost.

liam: acceptance criteria for the platform PR: policy schema + linter + canary toggles + metric alerts + console toggle + audit log entry on every spillover decision. + docs for sales/CS.

maya: actionables: @olivia prototype modal, @elaine add telemetry tags/metrics, @liam wire canary automation, @sam add legal override check and privacy checklist. i'll draft the policy RFC tonight and link it here.

olivia: noted. will start a small Figma for modal + settings page.

sam: i'll pull legal contract list and add `legal_restrict=true` tenants to staging for test.

maya: thanks — if anyone else wants to test policy permutations ping me. let's keep the initial rollout conservative (no more than 25% qps to hosted). :thumbsup:
